title: A Rapid, High-Resolution Chromatographic Method for Isolating Subpopulations of HEK293-derived Extracellular Vesicles
author: Ewonde, Raphael Ewonde
materials: Trilobal PET C-CP fiber microbore columns

Ammonium sulfate (≥99.0%), disodium hydrogen phosphate (≥99.0%), sodium dihydrogen phosphate (≥98.0%), sodium hydroxide, and Amicon Ultra-15 (10 kDa MWC) spin vials were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich (Spruce Street, MO, USA). HPLC-grade acetonitrile (ACN) was purchased from VWR Chemicals (Radnor, PA, USA), and Ultrapure water was produced in-house using an ELGA LabWater purification system (PURELAB flex, High Wycombe, UK). Carbon-coated 200 mesh grids and uranyl acetate were purchased from Electron Microscopy Sciences (Hatfield, PA, USA).

HIC experiments were performed on a Vanquish Flex UHPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Sunnyvale, CA, USA), consisting of a quaternary pump F, a split sampler FG, a UV-Vis photodiode array detector VF equipped with a 13 µL flow cell, and an integral fraction collector FT. Viper MP53N tubing was used to connect the different UHPLC modules. Samples were maintained at 5 °C in the autosampler and fraction collector. The injection volume was set at 4 µL, and the flow rate was set at 0.5 mL min-1, unless stated otherwise. Optical absorbance data were recorded at a wavelength of 216 nm, at a sampling rate of 5 Hz and a response time of 1 s. Chromeleon software (version 7.3.2) was used for instrument control and data management.

steps.title: Prepare cell culture supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect HEK293‑F culture supernatant, centrifuge at 700 × g for 5 min to remove cells, filter the supernatant through a 0.2 µm PES filter, aliquot 2 mL portions into tubes, store at –80 °C, and record the EV concentration (~1.48 × 10¹¹ particles mL⁻¹).

steps.title: Prepare quaternary mobile phases
steps.instruction: Make four mobile phases using ultrapure water: MP‑A = 2 M ammonium sulfate in 50 mM phosphate; MP‑B = 1 M ammonium sulfate + 10 % ACN in 50 mM phosphate; MP‑C = 35 % ACN in 50 mM phosphate; MP‑D = 50 mM phosphate buffer. Adjust pH to 7.0 by mixing disodium hydrogen phosphate and sodium dihydrogen phosphate and adding 2 M NaOH as needed. Filter each phase through a 0.22 µm PES vacuum filter (500 mL).

steps.title: Assemble and condition PET C‑CP columns
steps.instruction: Pull eight rotations (528 fibers) through 0.76 mm‑ID PEEK tubing, trim to 30 cm length; prepare 15 cm micro‑bore columns similarly and cut in half. For analytical runs, pack a 15 cm column (2.1 mm ID) with 40 fiber rotations. Condition the column by flushing 10 min with 100 % MP‑C, then 10 min with 100 % MP‑D, then equilibrate 5 min with 100 % MP‑A. Store at room temperature. After ~12 injections, flush fibers out with water at 6–8 mL min⁻¹ (outlet open) and replace with fresh fibers; also replace fibers after each set of successive injections.

steps.title: Set up UHPLC system
steps.instruction: Configure a Vanquish Flex UHPLC (quaternary pump, split sampler, PDA detector with 13 µL flow cell, fraction collector) using Viper MP53N tubing. Keep samples and collector at 5 °C. Set injection volume to 4 µL, flow rate to 0.5 mL min⁻¹ (unless changed later), record absorbance at 216 nm (5 Hz sampling, 1 s response). Control the system with Chromeleon v7.3.2.

steps.title: Run generic step gradient HIC
steps.instruction: Inject the prepared sample and apply the following gradient: Segment 1 – 100 % MP‑A for 2 min (captures proteins and EVs, early media components elute with injection); Segment 2 – 100 % MP‑B for 3 min (elutes retained culture proteins); Segment 3 – 100 % MP‑C for 3 min (elutes target EVs). Collect fractions with the integrated fraction collector.

steps.title: Run switchback gradient HIC (optimized)
steps.instruction: Apply a multistep isocratic gradient in Segment 3: 60 % MP‑C for 1 min, 80 % MP‑C for 1 min, 100 % MP‑C for 1 min. Insert negative steps to improve resolution: after the 60 % step, drop to 30 % MP‑C before the 80 % step; after the 80 % step, drop to 60 % MP‑C before the final 100 % MP‑C step. Collect the three resolved EV fractions.

steps.title: Buffer‑exchange fractions
steps.instruction: Transfer each collected EV fraction into an Amicon Ultra‑15 10 kDa MWCO spin filter and centrifuge according to the manufacturer’s protocol to exchange into the desired downstream buffer.

steps.title: Analyze fractions by NanoFCM
steps.instruction: Calibrate the NanoAnalyzer (dual 488/638 nm lasers) with 0.25 µm fluorescent silica microspheres (2.17 × 10¹⁰ particles mL⁻¹) diluted 1:100 and with the SM16‑Exo nanosphere cocktail (68–155 nm). Dilute each EV fraction in 50 mM phosphate buffer, label with MemGlow 640 dye (1:2500) and ExoBrite CD9/CD81 antibodies (1:4000), incubate at 37 °C for 3 h in a water bath. Set sample delivery pressure >160 kPa and sampling pressure 1 kPa. Flush the system with the manufacturer’s cleaning solution and rinse the external capillary with water between samples. Acquire data for 30 s using nFCM Profession V2.0 software.

steps.title: Analyze fractions by NTA
steps.instruction: Using a Malvern NanoSight NS300, set camera level to 13–14 and frame rate to 25 fps. Load each fraction into the flow cell, run flow = 1000 (instrument units) for 20 s, then flow = 100 for 120 s. Acquire a 60‑s video at flow = 100, repeat for five replicates. Between samples purge the cell with DI water then 10 % IPA for 2 min each at flow = 1000, then push ~3 mL air to remove liquid. Set detection threshold per sample (5–10) to keep debris count <5 and particle count >30 per frame. Process data with NanoSight NTA 3.4.4 software.

steps.title: Prepare TEM grids
steps.instruction: Buffer‑exchange each whole‑peak fraction to 20 mM HEPES, pH 7.0. Place 10 µL of the fraction on parafilm, add 10 µL of 1 % uranyl acetate, mix by pipetting. Lay a carbon‑coated 200‑mesh grid face‑down on the droplet, incubate 15 s, blot excess with lint‑free paper. Store grids in a desiccator overnight. Image on a JEOL TEM with 200 ms exposure, NS15 camera, at 120 kV.
